Primary work stays on the freshest days: Monday drives strict One-Arm Pull-up quality and the heavy Back Squat exposure, Sunday carries the direct Overhead Press, Tuesday gives the lower-fatigue assisted unilateral pull work around MMA, and Friday stays intentionally low-cost next to hard sport. The weekly long run sits on Saturday so it does not interfere with Monday’s primary heavy squat day.

Weeks 2-4: squat load rises only if the prior week stayed inside the RPE caps, strict One-Arm Pull-up progresses through cleaner 2-rep priority work and better symmetry rather than extra volume, assisted One-Arm Pull-up progresses by less help, Overhead Press stays submaximal and readiness-led, and the long run builds before dropping back in Week 4.

If elbows or biceps tendon feel irritated, keep the strict One-Arm Pull-up rows to all singles that day and use slightly more help on Assisted One-Arm Pull-up. If shoulders feel beat up from MMA, keep Push Press crisp and submaximal or stop one set early. If knee or low-back fatigue is high before Friday, keep the listed low-cost Back Squat dose at the low end and drop the final accessory first.

Mon	[WARMUP] Back Squat	60-140 kg ramp	3	3	90 sec	N/A	Compact ramp sets only; keep jumps efficient.	
Mon	One-Arm Pull-up	Bodyweight	1	1-2 per arm	3 min	8	Priority set; earn 2 reps only if both sides stay clean and at least 1 rep shy of technical failure. Week 1 standard: establish the benchmark - every single starts from a dead hang, no kip or swing, and you finish each side with at least one clean rep still in reserve. Record how each side felt; this is the standard Weeks 2-3 have to beat.

Record how each side felt; this is the standard Weeks 2-3 have to beat.

Mon	Back Squat	160 kg	2	3	4 min	7.5	Back-off sets; up to 2 sets, stop after 1 if bar speed clearly falls or technique degrades.	
Mon	Push Press	RPE-selected load	3	4	3 min	7	Clear overload/drive exposure for vertical press without grinding; crisp leg drive and locked-out finish.	
Tue	[WARMUP] Assisted One-Arm Pull-up	Light assistance	2	1 per arm	60 sec	N/A	Brief patterning; weaker arm first.; Squat-and-reach x 6; Bodyweight squat x 8; Scapular pull-up 2 x 5-6; Band pull-apart x 10-12; Keep the warm-up specific and non-fatiguing.	
Tue	Assisted One-Arm Pull-up	Minimal assistance	2	1 per arm	2-3 min	6-6.5	Clean symmetrical doubles each side; use the least help that keeps full ROM and no twist. Recovery-first pulling microdose: technical adjacent-day exposure only, keep it at RPE 6-6.5 or easier and stop well before local fatigue.	
Tue	Dumbbell Bulgarian Split Squat	RPE-selected load	2	6 per side	2 min	7	Moderate support lower-body work; keep it controlled, not exhaustive, before MMA.	
Tue	Ring Hamstring Curl	Bodyweight	2	8	90 sec	7	Keep hips extended and curl the heels toward you under control; shorten the lever if needed.

Fri	Back Squat	145 kg	2	5	3 min	6.5	Volume/specificity exposure; keep this genuinely easy enough to coexist with hard MMA later.	
Fri	Weighted Chin-up	+50 kg	2	4	3 min	7	Bilateral support strength for One-Arm Pull-up; reduce load if elbows or grip are stale.	
Fri	Neck Isometric	Bodyweight	2	20 sec each direction	45 sec	6	Flexion, extension, and side holds with smooth gradual pressure.	
Sat	Run	Easy conversational pace	1	20 km	N/A	6	Long run; stay clearly below threshold, relaxed breathing, no fast finish.
